# Fairstay Managed Care Authorizations (`fairstay-managed-care-authorizations`)

Managed care authorizations against the nursing-home census: days with no authorization, levels that differ from the authorized level, days past the authorized count, authorizations about to end with no next one, and concurrent reviews due or overdue. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Managed Care Authorizations never submits authorization requests or clinicals to a plan.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Case management · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-managed-care-authorizations demo
npx -y fairstay-managed-care-authorizations mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow managed care residents, checked from 1 to 16 March 2026. Planted:

- R1301: covered every day, with a review on 20 March. Nothing to do.
- R1302: 10 days authorized and 16 days in the building, a review that was due 12 March, and an authorization ending 17 March with nothing after it.
- R1303: the census says REHAB HIGH, but the authorization is for REHAB MED, and a review is due 17 March.
- R1304: admitted 5 March, with the authorization starting 9 March.
- R1305: one authorization ends today and the next one starts tomorrow, so nothing is flagged.
- R1306 is on Medicaid and needs no authorization.

[`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `auths_check` | Match each managed care census day to an authorization and list gaps, then authorizations ending and reviews due. | runs |
| `auths_write_report` | Write auths-authorizations.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and auths-authorizations.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/auths). | runs |
| `auths_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `auths_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `auths_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `auths_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `plan_portal_submit` | Fairstay Managed Care Authorizations never submits authorization requests or clinicals to a plan. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `auths_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `census` (required) | Census under --root: residents, payers, levels and dates |
| `auths` (required) | Authorization log under --root: resident, payer, authorization number, from, to, level, days authorized, next review |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: warn_days, review_warn_days, auth_payer_types |
| `start` | First census day to check (YYYY-MM-DD, default the first of the as_of month) |
| `as_of` | Last census day to check and the date to look ahead from (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-managed-care-authorizations inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Census (`census`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Facility Name, Building, Location, Fac, Center |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Census Date |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `bed_status` | text | Bed Status, Status, Census Status, Action, Census Action, Leave Type |
| `room` | text | Room, Room Bed, Bed, Room/Bed, Unit |

### Authorization log (`auths`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `auth_number` (required) | text | Auth #, Auth Number, Authorization, Authorization Number, Auth ID, Reference # |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Auth From |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `days_authorized` | number | Days Authorized, Authorized Days, Days Approved, Approved Days, Units |
| `next_review` | date | Next Review, Review Date, Next Review Date, Concurrent Review |

## Settings file (`auths_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `warn_days` | Flag authorizations ending within this many days (default 3) |
| `review_warn_days` | Flag concurrent reviews due within this many days (default 2) |
| `auth_payer_types` | Payer types that need an authorization (default managed_care) |

## Memory

`auths_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `auths_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `plan_review_rule` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-managed-care-authorizations": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-managed-care-authorizations",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-managed-care-authorizations -- npx -y fairstay-managed-care-authorizations mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-managed-care-authorizations tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-managed-care-authorizations sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-managed-care-authorizations inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-managed-care-authorizations call auths_check '{"census":"<census>","auths":"<auths>"}'
fairstay-managed-care-authorizations eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-managed-care-authorizations demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
